name: answer_back_to_the_agent
title: Tasks · an agent made on call, and the answer to its question goes back to it

steps.say: keep a list of deals: the firm's name and the asking price
steps.reply:
I've made a "Deal list" table in a new Deals module. It has two fields: the firm's name and the asking price. The table is empty so far.

I assumed the price is in dollars. Tell me if you use another currency and I'll change it.

Send me the deals, for example "Acme Corp, 2.5M", and I'll add them.
I added Midwest HVAC to your deal list with an asking price of $900,000.

steps.say: make an agent called Deal Analyst that, when given a task about a deal, works it out from the deal's row, saves what it found on the row with its source, and asks me for anything the row doesn't have
steps.reply:
I made the Deal Analyst agent in your Deals module. It's on call, so it has no schedule and only works when you give it a task about a deal. I haven't run it yet because it has no task to work on.

When you give it a task, it will:
1. Find the deal's row in your deal list and work from what the row holds. Today that's the firm name and asking price, for example Midwest HVAC at $900k.
2. Look up anything that can be looked up, and save each finding on that row with its source. The source is "stated" if you said it, the page or document it came from, or "estimated" with what it assumed. It adds

steps.say: add a task on Midwest HVAC to ask the broker for 3 years of P&L, give it to the Deal Analyst and start it
steps.reply:
I added the task "Ask the broker for 3 years of P&L" to the Midwest HVAC row in your deal list, gave it to the Deal Analyst, and started it. The Deal Analyst should pick it up within the half minute. You can follow its runs on the task's page.

The Deal Analyst only prepares things. If it drafts a message to the broker, nothing is sent until you approve it.
